company: Penguin Solutions, Inc. (filed under SMART Global Holdings, Inc.)
_note_naming: At the 2024-05-15 cutoff the registrant was still 'SMART Global Holdings, Inc.' trading as SGH on Nasdaq; the FY2023 10-K and all pre-cutoff 10-Qs were filed under SGH. PENG ticker is the same registrant (CIK 1616533) under its later corporate name 'Penguin Solutions, Inc.' — the company was already using 'Penguin Solutions' as an umbrella IPS brand pre-cutoff (per 10-K Item 1). No name-change 8-K has been filed pre-cutoff.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In 2023, 2022 and 2021, sales to our ten largest end customers (including sales to contract manufacturers or ODMs at the direction of such end customers) accounted for 60%, 62% and 59% of net sales, respectively. In 2023, 2022 and 2021, we had one, three and one customer account individually for over 10% of our net sales.' (10-K Item 1, Customers) Also: 'Net sales to an IPS customer were [redacted% — XBRL tag indicates 12%] of total net sales in 2022. No other customers accounted for more than 10% of our total net sales in 2023, 2022 and 2021.' (10-K Note 14, Significant Customer)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify customer-concentration step-down (three 10%+ customers in 2022 -> one 10%+ in 2023). Mode B — derive: if FY22 had THREE 10%+ customers and FY23 has ONE, then two named customers (or customer groups) dropped below the 10% reporting threshold in a single year on a revenue base that GREW 3.3% — i.e., the surviving 10%+ customer absorbed share while two others materially shrank. Identify the IPS customer (likely Meta or a hyperscaler given Penguin Computing's HPC/AI focus and the FY23 IPS surge of +70% YoY) and look for evidence in subsequent 10-Qs that hardware order cadence is decelerating.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K silent on which IPS customer hit >10% in 2022 and what the FY23 surviving 10%+ customer's share was. Q1 FY24 10-Q (Dec 1, 2023 quarter-end): IPS net sales DOWN 43.7% YoY, 'primarily due to lower hardware sales.' Q2 FY24 10-Q (Mar 1, 2024 quarter-end): IPS net sales down 36.4% Q2 / down 40.0% first six months, again 'primarily due to lower hardware sales.' First six months FY24 IPS revenue: $259.6M vs $432.8M prior-year period = -$173.2M concentrated almost entirely in hardware. The FY23 10-K narrative emphasized 'IPS net sales increased by $308.7M, or 70.0%, primarily due to $172.7M of revenue from our Stratus acquisition in August 2022, as well as higher volumes of sales in our Penguin Computing business' — i.e., ex-Stratus, organic Penguin Computing growth in FY23 was $136M. The FY24 first-half decline of $173M wipes out the organic FY23 growth AND begins to erode the inorganic Stratus contribution. This is the leading-indicator pattern: the FY23 'breakout' IPS growth story was a one-period burst driven by an HPC/AI hardware customer cycle (likely Meta/Llama infrastructure or a similar hyperscaler) that did not repeat into FY24.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B dominant signal. The 10-K Item 1 customer narrative is written in growth-thesis mode ('IPS group has shown solid growth') without disclosing that the FY23 IPS growth was structurally lumpy — concentrated in one hyperscale HPC/AI customer's deployment cycle. Two of the three 10%+ FY22 customers dropping below 10% in FY23 is itself a Mode-B flag (two material customer relationships materially shrank in one year). The two subsequent 10-Qs filed pre-cutoff (Jan 2024 and Apr 2024) confirm the IPS hardware-orders cliff with the segment off 40% YoY on a half-year basis. The 10-K should have but did not include forward-cadence sensitivity for the one customer carrying 10%+ status — and management filing the 10-K on Oct 25, 2023 had over four weeks of Q1 FY24 visibility (Q1 ended Dec 1, 2023; 10-K filed Oct 25, 2023, so they had zero Q1 visibility — correction: 10-K filed for FY ending Aug 25, 2023, so the IPS cliff is signaled in Q1 FY24 10-Q, NOT concealed by the 10-K). The honesty failure is that the 10-K MD&A presented IPS as 'solid growth' without acknowledging the cyclical/lumpy nature that the segment's own definition ('revenue is tied to customer decisions as to the completion of delivery and system go-live events') implies.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On August 29, 2022, we amended our credit facility and borrowed an additional $300 million ... we amended certain covenants under the amended credit agreement.' (10-K MD&A) and 'The Amended Credit Agreement also includes the following financial maintenance covenants tested on the final day of each fiscal quarter: i. a First Lien Leverage Ratio of 3.25 to 1.00; ii. a Total Leverage Ratio of 5.00 to 1.00; provided, that commencing after the eighth full fiscal quarter after the Effective Date, such Total Leverage Ratio level will instead be 4.50 to 1.00 ... iii. an Interest Coverage Ratio of 3.00 to 1.00.' (10-K Debt note)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify covenant levels and that the Aug 2022 Incremental Amendment LOOSENED the First Lien Leverage covenant from 3.00x to 3.25x. Mode B — derive: the Aug 2022 amendment was an enabling amendment for the Stratus acquisition, NOT a distressed amendment — i.e., management actively negotiated MORE leverage capacity to fund an acquisition. However, the Total Leverage Ratio steps DOWN automatically from 5.00x to 4.50x 'commencing after the eighth full fiscal quarter after the Effective Date' of the original credit agreement (Feb 7, 2022 -> eighth quarter = Q3 FY2024 ending around June 2024). I.e., the covenant TIGHTENS by 0.50x at exactly the moment IPS revenue is collapsing, FY23 net loss was $188M, and the Stratus Earnout ($50M) was paid down in Q2 FY24. Verify TTM EBITDA cushion against the post-step-down 4.50x cap.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Debt Note + Q2 FY2024 10-Q Debt Note (March 1, 2024) + Q2 FY2024 income statement
rfm_tuples.M_value: Outstanding under Amended 2027 TLA: $551.6M as of Aug 25, 2023 -> $500.0M as of Mar 1, 2024 (i.e., $51.6M voluntary/scheduled paydown over two quarters, supported by Brazil divestiture proceeds). Effective interest rate 8.22% on the term loan (vs convertible coupons of 2.00%-2.25%) — i.e., the debt stack is mostly floating SOFR+ pricing. Penguin TTM continuing-operations net loss: FY23 $188M reported net loss combined with H1 FY24 net loss of $32.4M = TTM ex-Brazil net loss roughly $50-80M depending on Brazil reclassification (Brazil had been a contributor to earnings before write-down). The Total Leverage covenant step-down from 5.00x to 4.50x triggers in roughly Q3 FY2024 (May 2024 quarter end) per the 'eighth full fiscal quarter after Feb 7, 2022 Effective Date' clock — exactly the cutoff-period quarter. Pre-cutoff EBITDA: Q2 FY24 (Dec-Mar) segment operating income $26.5M (Memory $6.0M + IPS $22.3M + LED -$1.8M, less corporate); annualize cautiously to ~$50-80M EBITDA range when reversing non-cash items. With $500M term loan against $50-80M EBITDA, gross leverage is 6.3x-10x; net leverage (less $125M of cash netting cap) is ~5.0x-7.5x — these are estimated and likely ABOVE the 4.50x covenant if the step-down has triggered or is about to. The 10-K and both pre-cutoff 10-Qs do NOT disclose a specific covenant-cushion calculation or attest to current compliance in the post-Stratus-paydown / post-Brazil-divestiture configuration.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B dominant. The credit-agreement step-down clause is the single most important forward-dated financial event in the disclosure stack and neither the 10-K nor the Q1/Q2 FY24 10-Qs walk a reader through the exit-the-grace-period math. Management knows the date (eighth full fiscal quarter after Feb 7, 2022 = on or around May 2024) and they know the TTM EBITDA trajectory. The 10-K Risk Factor 'failure to comply with any of these covenants would cause a default' is generic boilerplate; honest disclosure would include a covenant-headroom sensitivity. NO 10-K language attesting to current covenant compliance was located. NO 10-Q language attesting to current covenant compliance was located. This is anomalous for a distressed name and is itself a Mode-B finding: most companies with healthy cushions affirmatively state 'we were in compliance with all covenants' (cf. HLIT pilot). PENG's silence on this point combined with the imminent covenant step-down and deteriorating EBITDA is the strongest forensic signal in the dossier.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We have a significant amount of goodwill. As of August 25, 2023, we had goodwill of $162.0 million, which represented 11% of our total assets ... We currently anticipate that the remaining goodwill of the Penguin Edge reporting unit of $16.1 million as of August 25, 2023 may become further impaired in future periods.' (10-K Risk Factor + MD&A). 10-K already booked $19.1M of Penguin Edge goodwill impairment in FY23 ($17.6M Q2 + $1.5M Q4); also $153.0M SMART Brazil held-for-sale impairment + $29.0M increase in Stratus Earnout fair value = $201.1M of acquisition-related charges in FY23 alone.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the goodwill remaining at Penguin Edge ($16.1M) and trajectory of carrying value. Mode B — derive: of the remaining $162M total goodwill, how much sits in IPS (where Stratus and Penguin Computing live)? IPS is the segment experiencing the revenue cliff (-40% first-half FY24). If IPS goodwill is the bulk of remaining goodwill AND IPS revenue is now collapsing, the next goodwill impairment trigger is the IPS reporting unit, not just Penguin Edge legacy.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note on Intangible Assets and Goodwill + Q2 FY2024 10-Q Goodwill rollforward
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q2 FY24 10-Q discloses Penguin Edge goodwill of $16.1M still intact as of March 1, 2024 — i.e., the 'may become further impaired' language from the 10-K had NOT yet triggered an additional Penguin Edge write-down through the 6-month mark. Stratus goodwill (subsumed within IPS) is the dominant remaining bucket post Penguin Edge writedown. Stratus acquisition price: $225M cash + $50M Earnout = $275M for a business generating ~$172M of acquired revenue in its first year. The Stratus Earnout was paid in full at $50.0M in Q2 FY24 (i.e., maximum performance achieved in the trailing 12 fiscal months ending Aug 25, 2023) — meaning Stratus EXCEEDED gross-profit targets in its first ownership year. Post Q2 FY24, IPS as a whole is in retreat (-40% first half), creating goodwill impairment exposure on the Stratus reporting unit's fair value. Neither pre-cutoff 10-Q discloses a Stratus reporting-unit goodwill sensitivity or interim impairment test.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B signal. The 10-K legitimately flags Penguin Edge remaining goodwill as 'may become further impaired' — this is honest forward disclosure. The Mode-B gap is silence on IPS/Stratus goodwill, which is the larger and more macroeconomically exposed bucket. Goodwill impairment is a non-cash event that doesn't trip covenants directly, but it does cascade into the deferred-tax asset (FY23 tax provision included 'tax addbacks for nondeductible goodwill impairment') and into the stockholders' equity base, which already absorbed the $153M Brazil write-down. The combination of Penguin Edge legacy goodwill 'may become further impaired' + IPS revenue cliff + Stratus reporting unit not stress-tested is a Mode-B disclosure-completeness gap rather than concealment.

rfm_tuples.R: '/s/ DELOITTE & TOUCHE LLP ... We have served as the Company's auditor since 2014.' (10-K Auditor Report) — Critical Audit Matters: (1) 'evaluation of performance obligations and the determination of the timing of recognition as performance obligations are satisfied in certain contracts within the IPS segment'; (2) 'assessment of whether the disposal group [SMART Brazil] meets the criteria as an asset held-for-sale and the determination of the amount of the associated impairment charge.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify auditor tier (Deloitte = Big 4, PCAOB Firm ID 34) and tenure (since 2014 = ~9 years through FY23). Mode B — derive: the IPS revenue-recognition CAM is the critical audit-judgment area. Given IPS is the segment now experiencing the -40% YoY hardware decline, the CAM identifies the exact area where management has the most discretion to time revenue. Look for whether any of the IPS revenue softness in Q1/Q2 FY24 might reflect a tightening of recognition timing (i.e., revenue that would historically have been pulled forward is now being deferred), or whether deferred-revenue / contract-liability balances are growing unusually.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Auditor Report + Q2 FY2024 10-Q Note on Contract Liabilities + Q2 FY2024 Balance Sheet
rfm_tuples.M_value: Auditor = Deloitte & Touche LLP since 2014 (Big 4, PCAOB Firm ID 34). 9-year tenure is mid-length, not auditor-shopping. NO material weakness disclosed in ICFR. NO restatement. NO going-concern qualification. Both CAMs are routine for an acquisitive technology company. Cleanest possible audit signal. Contract liabilities and customer advances data in the Q2 FY24 10-Q are not large enough to suggest revenue is being deferred to manage future quarters (no contract-liability spike). Deloitte's IPS revenue-recognition CAM remains in place but no procedural concerns surfaced.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Deloitte Big 4 with 9-year tenure and no material weakness is a clean baseline. The IPS revenue-recognition CAM is appropriate given the segment's deal-by-deal go-live cadence but no smoking-gun emerged. This is the framework's PASS calibration — the auditor relationship itself is not a distressed-firm signal.

rfm_tuples.R: 8-K filed May 14, 2024 (accession 0001193125-24-138236): 'On May 8, 2024, Ken Rizvi notified SMART Global Holdings, Inc. (the "Company") that after over three years as the Company's senior vice president and chief financial officer ("CFO"), he intends to resign to pursue another opportunity. His resignation will be effective June 30, 2024 and is not the result of any dispute or disagreement with the Company. Effective upon Mr. Rizvi's departure, Jack Pacheco, the Company's former CFO and current chief operating officer and president of Memory Solutions, will assume the role of interim CFO ... on an interim basis until the Company appoints a permanent successor.' Same 8-K Item 7.01: 'the Company reaffirmed its financial outlook for the third quarter of fiscal 2024.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify CFO departure timing (7 days before the 2024-05-15 cutoff) and the absence of a permanent successor named at the time of announcement. Mode B — derive: the predecessor CFO Jack Pacheco was the OUTGOING CFO who handed off TO Rizvi roughly three years prior, and is also COO + President of Memory Solutions — i.e., he is being asked to carry three roles on an interim basis. This is a fall-back to a known-quantity prior-CFO rather than a planned succession. The CFO turnover is occurring exactly as: (a) IPS revenue is in cliff mode (Q3 FY24 outlook reaffirmation aside), (b) the credit-agreement Total-Leverage step-down to 4.50x triggers, (c) the FY23 $188M net loss is fresh, and (d) the FY23 tax-valuation-allowance release of $49M is recent. Reaffirming Q3 outlook the same day as announcing CFO departure with no permanent replacement is a 'managed crisis communication' move.
rfm_tuples.M_value: CFO Ken Rizvi resigned May 8, 2024; effective date June 30, 2024 (52-day notice — modestly short). Interim CFO is Jack Pacheco, previously CFO of the same company (2011-2021), who is concurrently COO and President of Memory Solutions. No permanent successor announced. Departure language: 'not the result of any dispute or disagreement with the Company.' Same 8-K Item 7.01 reaffirms Q3 FY24 outlook (i.e., management's tone is 'orderly transition, business as usual'). Form 4 activity prior to cutoff: 23 Form 4 filings between Nov 2023 and May 2024. Confirmed sales: (1) Joseph Gates Clark (President LED Solutions) — 2,529 shares sold 04/24/2024 @ $17.93 weighted-avg under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 04/17/2023 (small, $45K, programmatic); (2) Form 4 of 02/22/2024 contained both 'S' (sale) and 'M' (option exercise) codes — likely a cashless exercise/sell-to-cover, not an open-market discretionary sale; (3) cluster of Feb 13, 2024 Form 4s (Penny Herscher, Sandeep Nayyar, Randy Furr et al.) appear to be 'A' director equity grants from the annual board comp cycle. NO CEO Form 4 sales in the pre-cutoff 6-month window. NO insider BUYING.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B dominant signal. The CFO departure 7 days before cutoff with a fallback-to-predecessor interim arrangement is the single most concrete management-stress signal in the dossier. The reaffirmation of Q3 outlook in the same 8-K is intended to dampen market reaction but a 'CFO resigns + no permanent successor + 52-day notice' configuration during a quarter in which (a) IPS is in -40% decline, (b) a credit covenant tightens, and (c) the prior-cycle Stratus Earnout was just paid out, is a Mode-B 'these things go together' pattern. The language 'pursue another opportunity' is standard exit-on-good-terms phrasing — credible deniability of distress motivation — but the structural pattern (no successor lined up, predecessor returning, three roles for one person) suggests the departure was not long-planned. Note: insider Form 4 selling is largely programmatic 10b5-1 and not a strong independent signal here, but the LACK of any insider buying during a -31.4% drawdown is also a Mode-B negative.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'IPS net sales increased by $308.7 million, or 70.0%, primarily due to $172.7 million of revenue from our Stratus acquisition in August 2022, as well as higher volumes of sales in our Penguin Computing business.' (10-K MD&A FY23 vs FY22). Q1 FY2024 10-Q (filed 2024-01-09): 'IPS net sales decreased by $92.1 million, or 43.7%, primarily due to lower hardware sales.' Q2 FY2024 10-Q (filed 2024-04-09): 'IPS net sales decreased by $81.0 million, or 36.4%, and by $173.2 million, or 40.0%, in the second quarter and first six months of 2024 compared to the same periods in the prior year, respectively, primarily due to lower hardware sales.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the claim-evolution arc from 10-K (FY23 +70% YoY IPS growth, hero segment) to Q1 FY24 10-Q (-43.7% YoY IPS) to Q2 FY24 10-Q (-36.4% Q / -40.0% half) — i.e., is the segment that the 10-K positioned as the growth engine the SAME segment now driving the consolidated revenue decline? Mode B — derive: subtract the FY23 Stratus inorganic contribution ($172.7M) from FY23 IPS growth ($308.7M) -> organic FY23 IPS growth was $136.0M, or roughly +30% YoY ex-Stratus. The FY24 first-half decline of -$173.2M IS LARGER than the organic FY23 growth — i.e., the entire FY23 growth narrative has reversed within two quarters, AND a portion of the inorganic Stratus base is also evaporating.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A (Results of Operations FY23 vs FY22) + Q1 FY24 10-Q (0001628280-24-000961) MD&A + Q2 FY24 10-Q (0001628280-24-015494) MD&A + Q2 FY24 segment operating-income table
rfm_tuples.M_value: IPS sales trajectory pre-cutoff (continuing operations, ex-Brazil): FY21 $344.8M -> FY22 $441.0M (+27.9% YoY pre-Stratus) -> FY23 $749.7M (+70.0% YoY including 4 quarters of Stratus) -> H1 FY24 $259.6M (vs $432.8M H1 FY23, -40.0%). Annualizing H1 FY24 gives ~$520M run-rate IPS, which would be -30% vs FY23. IPS segment operating income: H1 FY23 $69.6M -> H1 FY24 $40.2M (-42.3%). The Q2 FY24 10-Q narrative ('primarily due to lower sales from our Penguin Solutions business, partially offset by lower operating expenses mainly driven by personnel-related expenses due to lower headcount') confirms two simultaneous developments: (a) hardware revenue collapse and (b) headcount reductions to defend operating income — i.e., management is restructuring without a separate restructure-plan announcement of the type that would typically accompany a $173M revenue cliff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B claim-evolution signal — the strongest standard-priority-list finding (priority #6: claim evolution between 10-K and prior 10-Q). The 10-K's IPS growth narrative was the single most prominent operating-momentum claim and it reversed in the IMMEDIATELY-following quarter. While the 10-K filing date (Oct 25, 2023) precedes the Q1 FY24 quarter-end (Dec 1, 2023), management had FY24 budget-cycle visibility when writing the 10-K, and the Risk Factor language about IPS revenue being 'tied to customer decisions as to the completion of delivery and system go-live events' was inserted (or refreshed) in this 10-K — i.e., management knew the segment was lumpy. Honest disclosure would have included a forward-cadence sensitivity in the MD&A. The two pre-cutoff 10-Qs faithfully report the decline magnitude (they do not conceal), so this is a 10-K-framing critique rather than an active-misrepresentation finding.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 5: 'On April 5, 2022, we announced that our Board of Directors approved a $75 million share repurchase authorization ... As of August 25, 2023, the remaining dollar value of shares that may be repurchased under this authorization was $16.6 million. No shares were repurchased during the fourth quarter of 2023.' Convertible-note exchange Q2 FY23: 'On January 18, 2023, SGH entered into separate, privately negotiated exchange agreements with a limited number of holders of its 2.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2026 (the "2026 Notes") to exchange $150.0 million principal amount of the 2026 Notes for (i) $150.0 million in aggregate principal amount of new 2.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 (the "2029 Notes") and (ii) an aggregate of $15.6 million in cash.' (10-K Debt Note)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the capital-allocation sequence: $75M buyback authorization Apr 2022 -> $50M used through FY22 -> $13.8M in FY23 under buyback + $14.1M cash premium in convert exchange + $50M Stratus Earnout paid Q2 FY24 + ongoing term-loan paydown. Mode B — derive: management paid a $14.1M premium to push $150M of converts from 2026 maturity to 2029 maturity while ALSO maintaining a buyback program AND ALSO funding the Stratus Earnout — i.e., simultaneous defensive (maturity extension) and offensive (buyback, earnout) capital deployment while operating losses accumulated.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Debt Note + 10-K MD&A Liquidity + Q2 FY2024 10-Q Stockholders' Equity Rollforward + Q2 FY2024 Cash Flow Statement
rfm_tuples.M_value: Capital deployment Q2 FY23 (convert exchange): $15.6M cash paid as exchange premium + accrued interest, of which $14.1M was a true premium above par — i.e., management voluntarily destroyed $14.1M of shareholder value to extend a $150M maturity by 3 years. Buyback program: $75M auth (Apr 2022), $50M used FY22, $13.8M FY23 -> remaining $16.6M as of Aug 25, 2023. No Q4 FY23 buybacks. Q1 FY24 buybacks (per the 10-Q): repurchases of [amount in $ millions not extracted but indicated] in the first quarter of 2024 under the same authorization. Cash and cash-equivalents and short-term investments as of Mar 1, 2024 = $465.8M, of which $348.6M was held by subsidiaries outside the United States (i.e., ~75% of cash is offshore, with potential repatriation tax friction). Term loan principal paydown Aug 2023 -> Mar 2024: $551.6M -> $500.0M = $51.6M deleveraging, likely supported by Brazil divestiture proceeds.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B capital-allocation framing signal. The 2023 convert exchange — paying $14.1M premium to extend $150M maturity by 3 years — is a defensive move that management framed as routine refinancing. Combined with continued buybacks of declining magnitude (down from $50M FY22 -> $13.8M FY23 -> small Q1 FY24 amount) and the simultaneous $50M Stratus Earnout cash outflow in Q2 FY24, the capital-allocation pattern shows management absorbing every available defensive AND offensive cash demand against a deteriorating EBITDA backdrop. 75% of cash held offshore is a typical Cayman-domiciled-company feature but creates a friction layer between the headline $465.8M cash number and the actually-deployable US-onshore liquidity for debt service. Not a SEVERE finding because all individual components are disclosed; it is the AGGREGATE pattern that is under-framed.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In 2023, our tax benefit of $49.2 million and effective tax rate of 124.5% was different from the U.S. statutory tax rate primarily due to a release of the U.S. federal and state valuation allowance.' (10-K MD&A) + 'As of August 25, 2023, we had U.S. federal and state net operating loss carryforwards of $32.1 million and $41.9 million, respectively. ... In addition, we also have Section 163(j) interest expense carryforwards of $101.0 million from the acquisition of Stratus, which do not expire. ... Our net operating loss, tax credit and Section 163(j) interest expense carryforwards are subject to limitations per Sections 382 and 383 of the Code. We have experienced ownership changes in the past, and we may experience ownership changes in the future as a result of future transactions in our ordinary shares.' (10-K Risk Factors)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the FY23 valuation-allowance release magnitude. Mode B — derive: a deferred-tax-asset valuation allowance is released when management concludes it is 'more likely than not' that future taxable income will absorb the NOL — i.e., management's FY23 internal forecast had to support a return-to-profitability case to justify the $49M release. If FY24 trajectory invalidates that forecast (the segment that was supposed to drive future income — IPS — is now in -40% retreat), then a partial REINSTATEMENT of the valuation allowance becomes a non-cash hit in FY24 or FY25. Also: Section 382/383 ownership-change risk references a specific known cumulative-ownership-change tracking obligation; this is volatile during a -31.4% drawdown when 5% shareholders may be churning.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A Income Tax + 10-K Risk Factor Section 382/383 + 10-K Note on Income Taxes + Q2 FY2024 10-Q Income Tax line
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY23 effective tax rate 124.5% (tax benefit of $49.2M on a pre-tax loss). Without the valuation-allowance release, the FY23 pre-tax loss of approximately $237M (= $188M net loss + $49M tax benefit) would have flowed through as a roughly $188M net loss anyway (the VA release flattered the headline). Section 163(j) interest-expense carryforward of $101.0M from the Stratus acquisition is a particularly notable item — it implies Stratus had material disallowed interest expense pre-acquisition that PENG is now stuck warehousing. Section 382/383 limitations are flagged as a known risk; with the ticker down 31.4% in trailing 52 weeks, the shareholder base is by definition turning over. The Q2 FY24 10-Q does not appear to disclose a Section 382 ownership-change study or a partial valuation-allowance reinstatement.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B accounting-quality signal. The FY23 reported net loss of $188M is the BEST-CASE net loss because it INCLUDES a $49M favorable valuation-allowance release. A more comparable apples-to-apples net loss for trajectory analysis is closer to $237M pre-tax loss. The 10-K dutifully discloses the components and the Risk Factor flags Section 382/383 exposure, so this is not concealment — but the MD&A framing of the $188M headline as if it were the underlying loss rather than the VA-release-flattered figure is a Mode-B disclosure-completeness gap. The Section 163(j) interest-expense carryforward of $101M is unusually large for a single acquisition of $225M and suggests Stratus carried meaningful pre-acquisition interest-disallowance baggage that the 10-K does not separately quantify.

rfm_tuples.R: 'During the second quarter of 2023, we initiated a plan pursuant to which we intend to wind down manufacturing and discontinue the sale of certain legacy products offered through our Penguin Edge business by approximately the end of calendar 2024.' (10-K MD&A) + 'Other operating expense in 2023 included restructure charges of $7.0 million primarily for employee severance costs and other benefits resulting from workforce reductions, the elimination of certain projects across our businesses and other costs associated with the wind down of our Penguin Edge business. We anticipate that such activities will continue into future quarters and anticipate recording additional restructure charges.' (10-K MD&A)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the Penguin Edge wind-down scope and timeline. Mode B — derive: 'Penguin Edge' was the SMART Embedded Computing + SMART Wireless brand consolidation under the renamed Penguin umbrella — i.e., it represents the legacy embedded systems hardware that PENG acquired through the SMART Modular history. Discontinuing it 'by approximately the end of calendar 2024' means an entire product line is being exited mid-fiscal-2025 (PENG fiscal year ends August). The customers of Penguin Edge include government/defense (per Item 1 description: 'specializing in high-performance products for customers in government, health care, industrial and telecommunications applications'). Counterparty disclosure mirror: do government customers (e.g., DoD prime contractors) disclose Penguin Edge as a key supplier?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1 (Penguin Edge description) + 10-K MD&A Restructure + Q2 FY2024 10-Q Restructure Note
rfm_tuples.M_value: Restructure charges: FY23 $7.0M total + 10-K language that activities 'will continue into future quarters.' Q2 FY24 10-Q restructure charge: $3.3M (Q2) and $6.3M (H1 FY24) — i.e., the FY24 restructure run-rate is approximately $12.6M annualized, almost DOUBLE the FY23 $7.0M annual rate. This is consistent with both the Penguin Edge wind-down completion AND broader headcount reduction across IPS due to revenue compression. Counterparty disclosure mirror was not executed in this pilot for time reasons but would be a logical follow-on (search edgar_fts.query_fulltext for 'Penguin Edge' OR 'SMART Embedded' across DoD contractor 10-Ks at cutoff_date='2024-05-15' to see if anyone discloses Penguin Edge as a key supplier — likely returns hits at General Dynamics, Curtiss-Wright, or similar embedded/rugged-systems integrators).

Mode B — derive: the 2026 Notes remaining $150M ($300M originally less the $150M exchanged for 2029 Notes) mature February 2026 — i.e., ~21 months after the cutoff. The Amended 2027 TLA matures February 2027. The 2029 Notes mature February 2029. The 2026 Notes are the FIRST refinancing event on the runway. With $465.8M cash and ~$50-80M run-rate EBITDA, the 2026 Notes are theoretically refinanceable from cash, but doing so would deplete the cash buffer to roughly $315M ($465.8M - $150M), and would not solve the 2027 TLA $500M maturity 12 months later. Effectively, PENG needs to refinance the 2027 TLA before Feb 2026 (typical 12-month refinance window) — i.e., they need a successful term-loan refinancing in calendar 2025 starting from a position of declining EBITDA and a recently-departed CFO.

Cash + short-term investments at Mar 1, 2024: $465.8M (75% offshore). Estimated TTM EBITDA: ~$50-80M depending on adjustments. Effective interest rate on term loan: 8.22%. The 2027 TLA refinancing at maturity (Feb 2027 actual but practically needs to be addressed by mid-2026) is the larger and more sensitive event; with $500M to roll and EBITDA potentially impaired, that refinancing is the central forward-dated solvency risk.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B disclosure-completeness signal. The debt stack itself is honestly disclosed and the Risk Factor language is appropriately cautionary. The Mode-B gap is the lack of a maturity-stack visualization and refinancing-strategy framing in the MD&A — the 10-K leaves the reader to assemble the maturity wall and refinancing math themselves. Combined with the imminent covenant step-down (C2), the CFO departure (C5), and the IPS revenue cliff (C6), the debt-maturity sequencing is the slow-moving structural concern that pulls the other signals together. PENG is not in imminent default risk — $465.8M cash provides material runway — but the forward operational EBITDA trajectory needs to stabilize before the FY25-FY26 refinancing window for the equity to recover.

summary: PENG (filed as SMART Global Holdings) shows a textbook Mode-B pattern of TECHNICALLY-COMPLIANT-BUT-UNDER-FRAMED disclosure. The audit is clean (Deloitte Big 4, 9-year tenure, no going-concern, no material weakness) and the 10-K does not actively conceal — it simply leaves the reader to assemble three converging structural concerns: (1) a Total Leverage Ratio covenant step-down from 5.00x to 4.50x triggering at exactly the cutoff-period quarter, with NO explicit covenant-compliance attestation in any pre-cutoff filing — anomalous and the strongest single forensic flag; (2) IPS segment revenue collapse of -40% YoY in H1 FY24, reversing the entire FY23 'hero segment +70% growth' narrative within two quarters and gutting the segment that the FY23 net loss of $188M was meant to grow into; (3) CFO Ken Rizvi resigning 7 days before cutoff with the predecessor CFO returning as interim across three concurrent roles and no permanent successor named. Cash position remains healthy ($465.8M, though 75% offshore) and there is no imminent default risk, but the FY25-FY26 refinancing window (2026 Notes Feb 2026 + 2027 TLA Feb 2027) needs EBITDA stabilization that the IPS trajectory does not yet support. The FY23 reported net loss of $188M is also flattered by a $49.2M deferred-tax-asset valuation-allowance release that may reverse partially in FY24. Verdict: SHORT-tier — Mode-B-dominant honesty failures concentrated around forward covenant cushion and segment-trajectory framing, against a structurally weakening operating base.
verdict_reasoning: 4 SEVERE + 5 MODERATE + 1 PASS findings; covenant step-down + IPS cliff + CFO departure all forward-looking signals consistent with continued underperformance during the backtest window; honesty failures are framing/under-disclosure rather than active concealment, but the AGGREGATE pattern around the imminent covenant step-down with no attestation is the kind of forensic signal the framework is designed to detect.
